aliases: New York Academy of Sciences Junior Academy
organizer: The New York Academy of Sciences
eligible_countries: Open internationally; the programme reports participants across 100+ countries

age_range.constraint: Students cannot participate if they turn 18 during the challenge

prerequisites: Strong English proficiency; commitment of three to four hours each week during challenge periods; interest in STEM and in collaborating with international peers.
program_dates: Innovation Challenges run for 10 weeks and take place twice during the programme year (fall and spring)
application_window_verbatim: Applications opened April 1, 2026 and closed July 9, 2026; admission decisions sent by August 31, 2026
duration: 10-week challenge periods, preceded by a kick-off week
cost_note: Verbatim: 'None. The Junior Academy is completely free for participating students.'
selection_process: Verbatim: 'Every application undergoes a review to ensure passionate students are offered the opportunity to join.'
award_or_output: Students form international teams and design solutions to real-world problems under STEM mentors. Completers receive 'a certificate of completion and a complementary Young Membership to The New York Academy of Sciences.' Winning teams receive educational prizes (no travel required).
source_title: The Junior Academy — The New York Academy of Sciences

sources.title: The Junior Academy — NYAS
sources.supports: 13–17 age range and the turn-18 constraint, zero cost, 100+ countries, 3–4 hrs/week commitment, Fall 2026 application dates and decision date, 10-week challenge structure, certificate and Young Membership

research_notes: VERIFIED for the Fall 2026 cycle on the organizer's own page: age band, the explicit rule that a student may not turn 18 during a challenge, zero cost, international openness, weekly time commitment, application open/close dates, and decision date. STATUS AS OF 2026-08-21: the Fall 2026 window closed on 9 July 2026 and decisions were due by 31 August 2026 — so this record is current but not currently applicable; the spring cycle dates are NOT published and are left null rather than estimated. HIGHEST-VALUE ATTRIBUTES FOR ORYN: genuinely free, genuinely global, online, and open to 13-year-olds — one of very few research-category opportunities that a 14-year-old Turkish student can actually access. NOT VERIFIED: acceptance rate or selectivity (the page describes review, not competitiveness — no selectivity tier should be inferred), and whether parental consent is required for minors.

duration: Verbatim: 'Two-week, hands-on projects where students worked alongside researchers and industry professionals to make a meaningful contribution to the work of an organisation.'
award_or_output: A research placement working alongside professional researchers; stated student outcomes include applying classroom knowledge to real-world challenges and strengthening UCAS applications.
